edges.description: GOF variants drive sustained/spontaneous STAT6 pathway activation independent of, and hyperresponsive to, upstream IL-4/IL-13 cytokine input.
Hyperactive STAT6 signaling skews CD4+ T-cell differentiation toward the TH2 program while suppressing TH1 and TH17 responses.

Constitutive STAT6 activity is oncogenic in the B-cell lineage: the same DNA-binding-domain residues mutated in the germline (notably D419) are recurrently mutated somatically in follicular lymphoma, predisposing to B-cell lymphomagenesis.
TH2 cytokines (IL-4/IL-13) drive B-cell immunoglobulin class switching to IgE, the humoral effector arm of the allergic phenotype.
TH2 cytokines (IL-5) drive eosinophil expansion and tissue recruitment, the cellular effector arm of the allergic phenotype.
Reciprocal suppression of TH1/TH17 responses contributes to recurrent and severe infection susceptibility in some patients.
IgE-mediated hypersensitivity drives food allergy, anaphylaxis, and atopic end-organ manifestations.
Eosinophilic tissue infiltration drives eosinophilic gastrointestinal disease and other atopic end-organ manifestations.
TH1/TH17 suppression manifests clinically as recurrent skin, respiratory, and viral infections.
The lymphomagenic predisposition manifests clinically as B-cell lymphoma (follicular lymphoma, with reported transformation to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma).
Elevated IgE reports the type 2 / IgE class-switching effector arm.
Blood eosinophilia reports the eosinophil effector arm of the type 2 response.
Eosinophil count is a pharmacodynamic marker of the eosinophil effector arm: it falls with dupilumab or JAK-inhibitor therapy and may track treatment efficacy.
Elevated serum CCL24/eotaxin-2 reports STAT6-driven eosinophil chemotaxis.
